title: The Dolbeault Complex and Integral Solutions

items.title: Bigraded complex forms and the Dolbeault operators
items.statement: On an open U⊂ℂⁿ, each complexified smooth k-form has a unique sum of (p,q) components, p+q=k, with basis dzᴵ∧dbar zᴶ. Define ∂ and dbar by projecting d to bidegrees (p+1,q) and (p,q+1), equivalently by the Wirtinger coefficient formulas. Holomorphic chart changes preserve both types and the operators.
items.strategy: Use dz_j=dx_j+i dy_j and dbar z_j=dx_j−i dy_j as an invertible complex change of cotangent basis. Expand d coefficientwise in the unique wedge basis. Under a holomorphic transition, its differential is complex linear and its conjugate is conjugate linear, so pullback preserves type; naturality of d then makes the projections coordinate independent.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2
Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4

items.title: The d, partial and dbar identities
items.statement: For every smooth complex form on an open U⊂ℂⁿ, d=∂+dbar, ∂²=0, dbar²=0, and ∂dbar+dbar∂=0; ∂ and dbar obey the graded Leibniz rule.
items.strategy: The coordinate formula splits d into the two unique bidegrees. Expand d²=(∂+dbar)² and compare the independent (p+2,q), (p+1,q+1), (p,q+2) summands; invoke the published d²=0 theorem. Project the published graded Leibniz identity to each bidegree.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2
Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4

items.title: Stokes for complex forms on a bounded C1 Euclidean domain
items.statement: Assume AC. If D⊂ℝᵐ, m≥2, is a bounded C¹ domain and α is a complex-valued C¹ (m−1)-form up to its closure, then ∫∂D α=∫D dα with outward-normal-first boundary orientation and the C¹ surface trace.
items.strategy: Write α=Σ_j(−1)^{j−1}F_j dx₁∧⋯∧hat(dx_j)∧⋯∧dx_m, split F into real and imaginary parts, and compute dα=(div F)dV. The boundary pullback is F·ν dS by the outward-first convention. Apply the published bounded-C¹ divergence theorem to the two real vector fields. AC is used exactly to invoke its AC_omega measure and surface-integration interface.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2

items.title: The Cauchy–Pompeiu formula with fixed signs
items.statement: Assume AC. For a bounded plane domain D with C¹ boundary, f∈C¹(overline D), and z∈D, f(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫∂D f(ζ)/(ζ−z) dζ +(2πi)⁻¹∫D f_{bar ζ}(ζ)/(ζ−z) dζ∧dbar ζ. The area term is −π⁻¹∫D f_{bar ζ}(ζ)/(ζ−z)dA.
items.strategy: Excise the positively oriented small circle about z; the inner boundary of D minus that disc has negative induced orientation. Apply the C¹ complex Stokes lemma to f(ζ)dζ/(ζ−z). Its derivative is f_{bar ζ} dbar ζ∧dζ/(ζ−z). Let the radius tend to zero: the inner circle tends to 2πif(z), while the area kernel has integrable O(r⁻¹) singularity. Swap the wedge order to obtain the displayed plus sign and dζ∧dbar ζ=−2i dA.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2
Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4

items.title: Local Cauchy transform with smooth parameters
items.statement: Assume AC. Let P=D₁×⋯×Dₙ be a polydisc, choose k and a smaller closed coordinate disc Dk′⊂Dk. For smooth g on P, there is a smooth T_k g on a polydisc containing Dk′ in coordinate k with ∂_{bar z_k}T_k g=g there. If ∂_{bar z_l}g=0 for selected l≠k, the same equations hold for T_k g. For g∈C∞_c(ℂⁿ), the same operator with no cutoff is globally smooth, solves ∂_{bar z_k}T_k g=g, and commutes with ∂_{bar z_l} for l≠k.
items.strategy: Choose a compactly supported smooth cutoff χ(z_k) equal to one near Dk′ and extend χg by zero in the k-th variable. Define T_k g=(2πi)⁻¹∫ℂ χ(ζ)g(z_1,…,ζ,…,z_n)/(ζ−z_k)dζ∧dbar ζ. Translation ζ=z_k+η puts all target derivatives on the smooth compactly supported numerator, so dominated differentiation gives smoothness and parameter commutation. In particular ∂bar_k T_k g=T_k(∂bar_k(χg))=χg by compact-support Cauchy–Pompeiu. For globally compactly supported g, omit χ; the same differentiation and Cauchy–Pompeiu argument applies on every parameter slice and on all of ℂⁿ.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2

items.title: The normalized Bochner–Martinelli kernel
items.statement: For n≥1 and ζ≠z in ℂⁿ, set Ω_n(ζ,z)=((n−1)!/(2πi)ⁿ)Σ_{j=1}ⁿ overline(ζ_j−z_j)|ζ−z|^(−2n) dbarζ₁∧dζ₁∧⋯∧hat(dbarζ_j)∧dζ_j∧⋯∧dbarζₙ∧dζₙ. Use dx₁∧dy₁∧⋯∧dxₙ∧dyₙ and outward-first boundary orientation. This is an (n,n−1) form in ζ, smooth off the diagonal and locally integrable in top-degree pairings at ζ=z; Ω₁=dζ/(2πi(ζ−z)).
items.strategy: The wedge expression has exactly n holomorphic and n−1 antiholomorphic factors. Each coefficient is O(|ζ−z|^(1−2n)); polar volume contributes r^(2n−1)dr, so the absolute singularity is locally integrable. Pairwise wedge products yield Ω₁ and fix the sign; the sphere integral is normalized in the following theorem.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Jabbari, Notes for Analysis and Geometry of Several Complex Variables, §3.2

items.title: The Bochner–Martinelli formula for C1 functions
items.statement: Assume AC. Let D⊂ℂⁿ be a nonempty bounded open set with C¹ boundary (a bounded C¹ domain, connectedness not required), and f∈C¹(overline D). For z∈D, f(z)=∫∂D f(ζ)Ω_n(ζ,z)−∫D dbar_ζ f(ζ)∧Ω_n(ζ,z). For holomorphic f the interior term vanishes; when n>1 the boundary kernel need not be holomorphic in z.
items.strategy: For ζ≠z differentiate the explicit kernel: only the missing dbarζ_j term survives, and Σ_j∂_{barζ_j}(overline w_j/|w|^{2n})=n|w|^(−2n)−n|w|²|w|^(−2n−2)=0. All dζ_j are present, so d(fΩ)=dbar f∧Ω. Apply C¹ Stokes to D minus B_ε(z); the inner sphere has negative induced orientation. Compute ∫∂Bε Ω=1 by differentiating the numerator form and using vol Bε=πⁿε^(2n)/n!. The f−f(z) sphere term is O(ε); the volume singularity is integrable. Let ε→0. AC is used through C¹ Stokes.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 5 §5.1
references.locator: Theorem 5.1.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 157–159 (PDF pp. 156–158), lines 12140–12476. Its smooth hypotheses are weakened here using the authored C1 Stokes supplier.

items.title: The local Dolbeault lemma on nested polydiscs
items.statement: Assume AC. If P′⊂⊂P are finite polydiscs in ℂⁿ and η is a smooth dbar-closed (p,q) form on P with q>0, then there is a smooth (p,q−1) form u on P′ satisfying dbar u=η|P′.
items.strategy: For a nonzero closed residual, split off the largest barred coordinate k as dbar-z_k wedge tau plus theta. Compare unique coefficients in dbar eta=0 to prove each coefficient of tau has zero dbar derivative in every later coordinate. Apply the local parameterized Cauchy transform coefficientwise in coordinate k; it solves the k equation and preserves those later zero derivatives. The remaining dbar derivative has only barred indices below k. Subtract it to obtain a closed residual with smaller maximal barred index, using dbar squared equals zero. Each coordinate is transformed at most once, and each local output domain still contains P-prime. After finitely many steps the residual has positive barred degree but no barred factors, hence is zero; sum the primitives. AC is declared for the local-transform premise.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.4, Lemma 4.4.7
references.locator: Complete proof, printed p. 143 (PDF page index 142), lines 11547–11620. The source treats concentric polydiscs; this item proves the stated coordinatewise compact-containment form. Exercise 4.4.14 at lines 11561–11562 is only a prompt; the coefficient-derivative assertion is proved here.

items.title: Compactly supported dbar solutions on complex Euclidean space
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥2, every smooth compactly supported dbar-closed (0,1) form g=Σ_j g_j dbar z_j on ℂⁿ has a unique smooth compactly supported u with dbar u=g. The solution vanishes on the unique unbounded connected component of ℂⁿ minus supp g.
items.strategy: Set u=T_1g_1 by the whole-plane Cauchy transform. Smoothness follows from translation of its locally integrable kernel. The coefficient identities from dbar g=0 and parameter commutation reduce every remaining equation to a compactly supported one-variable slice; Cauchy–Pompeiu on a large disc with zero boundary data gives ∂bar_j u=g_j. Bound supp g in a centered Euclidean ball. The exterior is connected in real dimension 2n≥4, and the defining integral vanishes on an open half-space Re z_2>R in its unbounded component. Holomorphy and the identity theorem force u to vanish throughout that component, so supp u is compact. The difference of two compactly supported solutions is entire holomorphic and vanishes on an exterior open set.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.2
references.locator: Theorem 4.2.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 132–134, PDF lines 10838–10967. The source uses the Cauchy transform and identity theorem; its Exercise 4.2.2 is only a prompt about differentiation under the integral, supplied here by the earlier fully proved transform lemma.

items.proof_strategy: From dbar g=0, extract coefficient compatibility by the type formula. Compact support of g puts each coefficient in C_c∞. Under AC define u=T_1g_1; the whole-plane transform lemma gives smoothness, the first equation, and commutation. For j>1, swap derivatives by compatibility and apply Cauchy–Pompeiu on a disc containing the compact slice to obtain g_j. Bound supp g in a Euclidean ball, prove its exterior connected in real dimension 2n≥4, and use the zero integral on an open coordinate half-space plus the identity theorem to show u vanishes on the unique unbounded component of the complement. The same bound gives compact support. Two compactly supported solutions differ by an entire holomorphic function vanishing on an exterior open set.

items.title: Hartogs extension by a compact-support dbar correction
items.statement: Assume AC. Let n≥2, Ω⊂ℂⁿ be a domain, K⊂⊂Ω compact, and Ω∖K connected. Every f∈O(Ω∖K) extends uniquely to F∈O(Ω), with no finite-shell-cover assumption.
items.strategy: If K is empty, extend f by itself. Otherwise the norm attains a maximum r on K. At a maximizer z₀, choose ε>0 with B(z₀,ε)⊂Ω; moving ε/2 outward when r>0, or taking (ε/2)e₁ when r=0, gives w∈Ω with |w|>R:=r+ε/4. Choose χ equal to one near K with support in Ω∩B_R. Define f₀=(1−χ)f on Ω∖K and zero on K; it is smooth on Ω. Set g=dbar f₀ on Ω and extend only this compactly supported form by zero outside Ω. Then g=−f dbarχ on Ω∖K, is closed, and is supported in B_R. Solve dbar u=g using compact-support solvability. Radial paths and rescaled paths on S^{2n−1} make {|z|>R} connected and unbounded; it therefore lies in the unique unbounded component of ℂⁿ∖supp g, where u vanishes. The nonempty open set Ω∩{|z|>R} lies in Ω∖K, where h=u+χf is holomorphic and vanishes. Connectedness and the identity theorem give h=0 throughout Ω∖K. Thus F=f₀−u is holomorphic on Ω and equals f on Ω∖K; uniqueness follows from the identity theorem. Full AC is used for the cited solution theorem.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.3, Theorem 4.3.1
references.locator: Complete theorem and proof, printed pp. 135–136, PDF lines 10987–11044. Exercises 4.3.1 and 4.2.3 are prompts; the bump and compact-support suppliers cited here provide the needed arguments.

items.title: Dolbeault cohomology of a domain
items.statement: For an open U⊂ℂⁿ, define H^{p,q}_{dbar}(U)=ker(dbar:Ω^{p,q}(U)→Ω^{p,q+1}(U))/im(dbar:Ω^{p,q−1}(U)→Ω^{p,q}(U)), with Ω^{p,−1}=0. Because dbar²=0 this quotient is well defined. Holomorphic restrictions U′⊂U induce maps on classes by restricting representatives, independently of representatives and compatibly with composition.
items.strategy: Use dbar²=0 for im⊂ker. The coordinate formula commutes with restriction, so closed and exact forms restrict to closed and exact forms; check the quotient universal property and identity/composition of restriction. No identification with sheaf cohomology is asserted.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4

items.title: Positive-degree Dolbeault cohomology vanishes on a polydisc
items.statement: Assume the full axiom of choice. Let n≥1 and P=∏_{j=1}^n D_j⊂ℂⁿ, where each D_j is a nonempty open disc of finite positive radius or is ℂ. For integers 0≤p≤n and 1≤q≤n, every smooth dbar-closed η∈Ω^{p,q}(P) is dbar-exact; hence H^{p,q}_{dbar}(P)=0.
items.strategy: For each finite-radius factor D(a,R), set D_k=D(a,(1−2^(−k))R); for each ℂ factor set D_k=D(0,k). Their products P_k exhaust P and have compact closures nested in P_{k+1}. The local Dolbeault lemma supplies primitives on successive larger P_k. For q>1, given ω_k on P_{k+2}, take a new primitive σ on P_{k+3}; the closed difference ω_k−σ on P_{k+2} has positive barred degree, so solve it on P_{k+1}. A bump supported in P_{k+1} and equal to one near the closure of P_k corrects σ by dbar of the cut-off primitive. This gives ω_{k+1}=ω_k on P_k and preserves dbar, so the sequence glues smoothly. For q=1, the coefficients of σ−ω_k on P_{k+2} satisfy every Cauchy–Riemann equation by unique wedge coefficients, hence are holomorphic. Apply the several-variable power-series theorem on a larger centered polydisc and approximate the finitely many coefficients on the compact closure of P_k by holomorphic polynomials with maximum error below 2^(−k). Subtract that polynomial (p,0)-form from σ. The resulting primitives are locally uniformly Cauchy; for each fixed ℓ their differences from ω_ℓ are locally uniform limits of holomorphic coefficients on P_ℓ, so are holomorphic, smooth, and dbar-closed. Their limit is a smooth global primitive. The quotient definition then gives H=0. Full AC is stated and used for the local lemma and the countable recursive choices of primitives and corrections.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
references.locator: Chapter 4 §4.4, Theorem 4.4.5 and complete proof, printed pp. 141–145, PDF text lines 11318–11324 and 11626–11680. The source proves the q>1 gluing case and the q=1 scalar construction; its reduction of q=1 to p=0 cites Exercise 4.4.6, which is only a prompt. This item proves the q=1 argument directly for every p by applying the power-series construction to each of the finitely many form coefficients. The local input is Lemma 4.4.7, printed p. 143, lines 11547–11620.

Guillemin and Campbell, MIT 18.117 Lecture Notes, Lectures 1–4

title: The Dolbeault Complex and Integral Solutions: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Elementary partial and dbar calculations
items.statement: On ℂ², for f(z)=z₁² overline(z₂)+overline(z₁)², ∂f=2z₁overline(z₂) dz₁ and dbar f=2overline(z₁)dbar z₁+z₁²dbar z₂. For η=f dz₂, ∂η=2z₁overline(z₂) dz₁∧dz₂ and dbar η=(2overline(z₁)dbar z₁+z₁²dbar z₂)∧dz₂, with the dbar z₂∧dz₂ sign retained.
items.strategy: Apply the Wirtinger rules to the monomials and wedge the coefficient differential with dz₂. Check explicitly that dbar z₂∧dz₂=−dz₂∧dbar z₂, and that d=∂+dbar on the displayed η.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.4
references.locator: Definition 4.4.1, printed p. 137, PDF lines 11136–11164. It defines the type operators used here; this example and its coefficient calculations are derived locally.

items.title: A compact-support Cauchy–Pompeiu calculation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let f(z)=(1−|z|²)² for |z|<1 and f(z)=0 for |z|≥1. Then f∈C¹_c(ℂ), its boundary Cauchy term on the unit disc is zero, and the area term at z=0 equals f(0)=1.
items.strategy: Inside the unit disc ∂bar f=−2z(1−|z|²), while f and its first derivative vanish at the circle so zero extension is C¹. Evaluate the area term at zero as −π⁻¹∫_D [−2ζ(1−|ζ|²)]/ζ dA=(2/π)·(π/2)=1; the apparent quotient at ζ=0 is removable in the integral.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.1
references.locator: Theorem 4.1.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 130–131, PDF lines 10628–10751. This supplies the Cauchy–Pompeiu identity; the compactly supported function and integral evaluation below are an explicit application proved here.

items.title: Bochner–Martinelli on the unit ball
items.statement: Assume AC. On the unit ball B⊂ℂⁿ, the normalized kernel has ∫∂B Ω_n(ζ,0)=1 and ∫∂B ζ_j Ω_n(ζ,0)=0 for every j, matching the values at zero of 1 and z_j.
items.strategy: Apply the Bochner–Martinelli formula to the constant function to evaluate the normalized kernel integral as 1. For each coordinate moment, use the explicit kernel formula to compute its pullback under the orientation-preserving scalar rotation ζ↦e^{it}ζ: Ω_n(ζ,0) is invariant and ζ_j acquires e^{it}. The oriented-manifold change-of-variables theorem then forces the moment integral to vanish. These calculations give the constant and coordinate-function reproduction values at zero.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 5 §5.1
references.locator: Theorem 5.1.1 and its complete proof, PDF lines 12140–12476 (Chapter 5 printed pp. 157–159). This example applies the formula to the constant and independently computes coordinate moments by rotations.

items.title: A polynomial closed form and its potential
items.statement: On ℂ², g=2overline(z₁)dbar z₁+z₁ dbar z₂ is dbar-closed and u=overline(z₁)²+z₁ overline(z₂) satisfies dbar u=g.
items.strategy: Differentiate each polynomial coefficient. The two cross derivatives ∂bar₂(2overline z₁) and ∂bar₁(z₁) both vanish, so dbar g=0; direct Wirtinger differentiation of u gives exactly the two coefficients. This is a choice-free calculation.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.4
references.locator: Definition 4.4.1, printed p. 137, PDF lines 11136–11164, defines the coefficient operators used here. The specific polynomial form and potential are constructed and computed in this item.

items.title: A nonclosed dbar form cannot have a potential
items.statement: On ℂ², g=overline(z₁)dbar z₂ has dbar g=dbar z₁∧dbar z₂≠0; hence there is no smooth u with dbar u=g on any nonempty open subset.
items.strategy: Compute dbar g from the coefficient derivative, noting dbar z₁∧dbar z₂ is a nonzero local basis element. If g=dbar u then dbar g=dbar²u=0 by the already proved identity, contradiction at every point.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapter 4 §4.2
references.locator: Exercise 4.2.1, printed p. 132, PDF lines 10832–10837. It asks for an explicit non-solvable (0,1)-form in C² but gives no witness or proof; the witness and local obstruction below are derived here.

items.title: Cutoff extension across a puncture in complex dimension two
items.statement: Assume full AC. Let G=B(0,2)∖{0}⊂ℂ² and let f be holomorphic on G. Choose a smooth χ with χ=1 near 0 and supp χ⊂B(0,1). Set f₀=(1−χ)f on G and f₀(0)=0; extend g=dbar f₀ by zero outside B(0,2), and let u be the compactly supported solution of dbar u=g. Then F=f₀−u is holomorphic on B(0,2) and equals f on G. For the concrete input f≡1, this construction returns F≡1.
items.strategy: Use the compact-set bump lemma at {0}; its support is closed and bounded inside B(0,1), hence compact. Since χ=1 near 0, f₀ is smooth across 0. On G, dbar f=0 and dbar f₀=−f dbarχ, so g is a smooth compactly supported closed (0,1)-form supported inside B(0,1); zero extension is smooth because the support stays away from ∂B(0,2). The compact-support theorem applies under full AC and its unique unbounded-component conclusion gives u=0 on {||z||>1}: that exterior is connected and unbounded in ℂ²∖supp g. Thus h=u+χf is holomorphic on G and vanishes on the nonempty open annulus 1<||z||<2. Prove G is connected by radial paths to the unit sphere and path-connectedness of S³; the identity theorem gives h=0 on G. Therefore F=f on G, while dbar F=0 on B(0,2) proves F holomorphic there. For f=1, g=−dbarχ and h=u+χ=0 on G, so u=−χ there and F=1 on G; continuity gives F(0)=1.

references.title: Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, v4.4, Chapters 4–5
references.locator: Chapter 4 §4.3, Theorem 4.3.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 135–136, PDF text lines 10987–11043. The source's Exercise 4.3.1 (cutoff existence) and Exercise 4.2.3 (support of the compact solution) are prompts, not proof text; the local bump and compact-support theorem suppliers plus the explicit exterior-component argument below provide those steps.
